paper_core_claims.claim: HotMoE inserts a sparse mixture of rank-8 LoRA experts into feed-forward projections of a frozen Qwen2-1.5B backbone and activates the top two of five experts per token.
Lower-half layers use attention among global expert embeddings to encourage shared expert relations, while upper-half layers use input-adaptive token-expert attention for task-specific selection.
A similarity-guided auxiliary loss encourages similar hidden states to have similar routing distributions and dissimilar states to diverge, combined with negative GJS and language-model loss.
MRD averages each multi-task model's relative per-task change against separately tuned rank-8 LoRA baselines, exposing seesaw tradeoffs that a raw average can hide.
Averaged over three runs, HotMoE reports the best MRD in the selected synergy (+1.68%) and conflict (+0.25%) scenarios with 3.19% trainable parameters.
Routing and loss ablations lower MRD in the selected scenarios, and adding the similarity term improves AVG/MRD for the tested standard router and MoLORA variants.

function_concept_used_by_paper: A function is a conditional low-rank residual transformation attached to a frozen base-model projection. Five learned LoRA experts form a bank, and a learned token-level router selects and weights the top two deltas. The overall runtime function is the frozen base model plus layer-specific mixtures of these residual experts. It is not an independently specified symbolic function, and individual expert semantics are emergent rather than contractually named.
specification_language: Training samples contain an instruction, task-specific context and output target across a fixed collection of NLP datasets. The optimization specification is language-model loss plus routing regularizers; MRD compares multi-task performance against separate per-task LoRA baselines. There is no explicit contract for each expert, no type/effect schema, pre/postconditions, negative constraints, safety policy, resource SLA, ambiguity resolution or compatibility/version declaration.

representation_or_carrier.expert: Each expert is represented by two learned low-rank matrices whose residual output modifies a selected feed-forward projection.
representation_or_carrier.router: Lower layers carry global expert embeddings and expert-expert attention; higher layers add hidden-state-conditioned expert embeddings and token-expert attention.
representation_or_carrier.artifact: Trainable adapter/router state plus configuration attached to the exact base model and target-module layout.
representation_or_carrier.boundary: Experts are jointly trained numerical deltas. The paper does not give them stable semantic identifiers, standalone interfaces, independent tests or portability beyond the covered backbone/module schema.

compiler_or_generator.training: Joint multi-task instruction tuning freezes the backbone and optimizes LoRA matrices, expert embeddings, routers and the similarity/GJS auxiliary objective.
compiler_or_generator.selection: The learned routing function produces a probability vector per hidden state, takes the top two experts and combines their residual outputs.
compiler_or_generator.output: A base-bound HotMoE checkpoint with approximately 3.19% trainable parameters in the reported setup.
compiler_or_generator.classification: This is a stochastic approximate training/generation process for a routed adapter artifact, not a semantics-preserving compiler from task descriptions to verified functions.

interpreter_or_runtime: At each targeted feed-forward layer, the fixed base projection runs and the layer-appropriate router computes attention-refined routing weights. Only the top-two LoRA expert residuals are weighted and added to the base output. Fixed weights, input and numerical environment yield a deterministic forward pass, but training, data order and generation can be stochastic. The implementation may cache lower-layer expert-expert attention during evaluation.
state_or_effect_model: Runtime state consists of token hidden states, global/input-adaptive expert embeddings, routing probabilities, selected expert indices and Transformer activations. Training additionally accumulates batch routing/hidden-state statistics for auxiliary loss. No external effects, authority, filesystem/network action contract, transaction, exception, idempotence, compensation, rollback or safety sandbox is modeled.
composition_rule: Composition is conditional residual addition: a frozen base linear map plus a weighted sum of top-k low-rank expert outputs. Routing differs by layer depth, with expert-expert attention below the midpoint and token-expert attention above it. This is neither static adapter arithmetic nor a demonstrated algebra for independently trained adapters; the experts are jointly trained and base/shape coupled.

equivalence_notions.notion: task performance relative to single-task adapters
equivalence_notions.support: MRD averages normalized per-task score changes against separately trained rank-8 LoRA baselines.
equivalence_notions.boundary: Positive MRD is a benchmark aggregate, not behavioral equivalence, dominance on every task or preservation of the base model.

equivalence_notions.support: Cosine similarity between hidden states is used as a proxy to make routing distributions similar or different.
equivalence_notions.boundary: Hidden-state cosine similarity is not a ground-truth task ontology, expert-capability proof or calibrated routing correctness criterion.

equivalence_notions.support: Replacing hybrid routing or removing loss terms lowers selected aggregate metrics in reported settings.
equivalence_notions.boundary: Ablations are averaged point results without uncertainty and do not identify a unique causal mechanism across other backbones or task mixes.

validation_regime.base_and_tasks: Qwen2-1.5B across seven unique benchmarks: MRPC, RTE, HellaSwag, CommonGen, WMT19 English-to-Chinese, ARC-C and BoolQ.
validation_regime.scenarios: Five-task synergy and five-task conflict mixtures with overlapping RTE, CommonGen and WMT19 tasks.
validation_regime.metrics: Accuracy for five classification tasks, BLEU for WMT19, ROUGE-L for CommonGen, raw average and the paper-defined MRD.
validation_regime.main_results: HotMoE reports AVG/MRD 55.38/+1.68% in synergy and 54.05/+0.25% in conflict, averaged over three runs. It is not best on every per-task metric; rank-40 LoRA has higher synergy AVG 56.13 and HydraLoRA has slightly higher conflict AVG 54.15.
validation_regime.ablations: Standard-router replacements, lower/higher routing replacements, removal of GJS/similarity terms and transfer of the similarity loss to Wg/MoLORA are compared.
validation_regime.parameter_budget: Five rank-8 experts, top-2 routing, midpoint split r1=0.5, expert/router dimensions 256 and auxiliary coefficients βc=1, βd=1.5, γ=0.01.
validation_regime.uncertainty: The paper says all main-table results average three runs but gives no standard deviations, confidence intervals, significance tests, individual seeds or per-run values. Ablation-run repetition is not separately stated.
validation_regime.artifact: The repository lacks the seven-task data manifest, official evaluation scripts, raw runs and checkpoints needed to reproduce Tables 1-5. The paper-referenced appendices with further setup are absent from the canonical PDF.
validation_regime.safety: No harmful-output, bias, privacy, robustness, adversarial routing, expert-collapse under distribution shift or operational safety evaluation is reported.

uncertainty_model: Routing weights are categorical-like softmax scores truncated to top two, and training is stochastic; however, the scores are not calibrated probabilities of task suitability or correctness. Main results average three runs but omit dispersion and seeds. There is no predictive uncertainty, router-confidence calibration, entropy threshold, abstention/fallback policy, out-of-distribution detection, expert-collapse alarm or risk bound for a new task mixture.
lifecycle_and_provenance: A governed routed-adapter artifact would bind the base-model hash/license, target modules, expert count/rank, layer split, router/loss settings, task datasets/splits, prompt formatting, seeds, dependencies/hardware, code commit, checkpoint format/hash and per-task/aggregate evaluation receipts. The paper gives part of this configuration, while the repository has only three commits, no license/tag/release/checkpoint/results/full data, an incomplete publication-time head and a postpublication repair. The state file is mislabeled as safetensors despite torch.save serialization. No promotion, monitoring, routing-drift, expert-retirement, migration, compatibility or rollback registry is defined.

N1_FunctionSpec.reason: Instructions, contexts, targets and task metrics form an empirical objective, but experts have no explicit contracts or declared capability interfaces.

N2_Representation.reason: Low-rank expert matrices plus global/adaptive expert embeddings and routers are explicit base-bound numerical function carriers.

N3_Compiler.reason: Joint tuning generates a routed checkpoint, but it is approximate stochastic optimization without semantics-preserving compilation or correctness guarantees.

N4_Artifact.reason: The implementation defines save/config artifacts, but no trained checkpoint is released and publication-time/current format and completeness problems prevent an accepted immutable artifact.

N5_Interpreter.reason: The frozen base plus layer-aware top-k adapter forward pass is a concrete runtime.

N6_ExecutionTrace.reason: Routing weights and selected experts are observable in principle, but no standardized trace, stored routing log, causal attribution or replay receipt is released.

N7_Validator.reason: Per-task metrics, AVG, MRD and ablations provide an explicit empirical validator bounded to selected benchmarks; they are not semantic verification.

N8_ComposerRouter.reason: Layer-dependent expert-expert/token-expert attention and top-k weighted residual addition directly implement conditional routing/composition.

N9_VersionedRegistry.reason: No expert capability registry, compatible base/version matrix, immutable release or lifecycle governance is defined.

GAP-015.reason: Instruction/target datasets and metrics provide empirical task specifications, while absence of expert contracts exposes the remaining specification gap.

GAP-016.reason: HotMoE directly supplies conditional top-k composition and layer-aware routing over low-rank residual experts, bounded to jointly trained same-base modules.

GAP-017.reason: Per-task metrics and MRD explicitly validate tradeoffs relative to single-task adapters, though they do not establish semantic equivalence or universal dominance.

GAP-018.reason: Token/routing/training state is modeled, but no external effect, authority, failure or rollback semantics is present.

GAP-019.reason: Base, adapters, routers, data and metrics require joint provenance, while the released repository lacks an immutable complete publication receipt.

GAP-020.reason: Soft routing and three-run averaging expose uncertainty, but no dispersion, calibration, abstention, shift detector or fallback policy is supplied.

source_specific_reasoning: CONFIRMED is appropriate only for the bounded architectural claim: HotMoE jointly trains a same-base bank of low-rank experts and routes tokens through layer-dependent expert-expert or token-expert attention with a similarity-guided loss. 121CX assigns no credit to frozen arXiv:2402.11285 because its exact registered bytes are an unrelated O-RAN paper, and uses the exact AAAI-26 PDF repaired by 121CN while correcting the repair's 2025 venue year to 2026. The headline is narrowed to best MRD in two selected three-run scenarios: HotMoE does not win every task or even every AVG comparison. Static repository inspection confirms the method shape but cannot reproduce tables because the publication-time code was incomplete and the current repository lacks full data, evaluation, results and checkpoints.
confirmed_projection: The paper confirms a useful Function OS routing pattern: keep a shared base runtime, represent bounded increments as low-rank expert artifacts, choose them from token state through a layer-aware router, compose only a sparse top-k residual, and validate aggregate benefit without hiding per-task regressions. It also shows why a router needs an explicit capability/provenance registry and uncertainty/fallback policy before routing scores can be treated as governed function selection.
projection_boundary: This projection is based on the exact 9-page AAAI-26 PDF, every rendered page, complete extracted text, official landing/DOI metadata, exact frozen wrong-binding PDF/metadata and complete relevant repository/history inspection. Current core syntax was checked, but models, data and experiments were not run. This model review is not a proof, formal verification, causal proof of specialization, independent empirical validation, benchmark reproduction, calibrated router audit or validation of ignition.
what_the_paper_does_not_support: It does not support the frozen arXiv:2402.11285 binding, which is an unrelated O-RAN resource-allocation paper.
It does not describe adapter arithmetic or merging independently trained LoRA checkpoints; its five experts are jointly trained and conditionally mixed.
It does not give each expert an explicit semantic capability contract or guarantee that expert attention recovers true task structure.
It does not show HotMoE dominates every baseline on every task or every aggregate: rank-40 LoRA has higher synergy AVG and HydraLoRA has slightly higher conflict AVG.
It does not show that +1.68% or +0.25% MRD generalizes beyond the selected Qwen2-1.5B task mixtures.
It does not report run dispersion, statistical significance, routing calibration or predictive uncertainty.
It does not prove that hidden-state cosine similarity is a correct semantic or capability metric.
It does not establish base-behavior preservation, semantic equivalence, safety or robustness under task/distribution shift.
It does not define effects, permissions, sandboxing, transactions, rollback or an expert registry.
It does not release a complete executable publication-time code/data/checkpoint/evaluation/run bundle.
This review does not independently validate the reported benchmark results.
limitations_and_failure_boundaries: The study uses one 1.5B backbone and two hand-constructed five-task mixtures drawn from seven benchmarks.
MRD depends on the chosen single-task LoRA baselines, metrics and normalization; it is not comparable without identical baseline receipts.
A positive aggregate MRD can coexist with individual task regressions, as shown by the tables.
Results are averages of three runs without standard deviations, confidence intervals, significance tests or published seeds/per-run values.
The paper gives no inference latency, memory, throughput or routing-overhead measurement despite the parameter-efficiency framing.
Top-2 of five and a 0.5 layer split are selected settings; general behavior for more experts, other ranks, routers, backbones or task counts is not established.
Hidden-state similarity can reflect nuisance factors and may cluster semantically distinct tasks or separate related ones.
Relaxing load balance can create underused or overloaded experts; the referenced Appendix E.3 analysis is absent from the canonical PDF.
No expert-collapse, adversarial routing, long-context, multilingual-beyond-one-translation-pair or out-of-distribution study is included.
Appendices A-E referenced for GJS, preliminary analysis, baseline/data details and extra ablations are not present in the reviewed PDF/landing page.
The code available at publication was missing hotmoe/config.py and therefore could not satisfy its own import path.
The current repository has no test suite, CI, tag/release, license, full seven-task data, evaluation scripts, raw results or trained checkpoint.
The training shell contains an unresolved model placeholder that breaks direct execution, and requirements contain machine-local conda URLs.
Released data building takes the first examples and performs an unshuffled 90/10 split, which does not document official benchmark-test reproduction.
The released trainer evaluates language-model loss, not the paper's accuracy/BLEU/ROUGE-L/MRD pipeline.
Checkpoint bytes are produced by torch.save while named .safetensors, increasing format/provenance ambiguity.
No model/data license and dependency-license aggregation is provided for the large vendored code tree.
The old 121B wrong source binding again shows that DOI/title/hash identity must be checked jointly before semantic credit.
